what: Victory Capital runs investment funds through a set of separately branded investment teams, each keeping its own process, on one shared operating platform, and it bought Amundi's American business in 2025.
customers: Financial advisers, retirement plans and institutions investing in its mutual funds and ETFs.
money: fees on assets in funds and separate accounts
moat: A shared platform for distribution, compliance and operations that lets small investment teams keep their autonomy while running at a cost ratio they could not achieve alone.
risks: Active management keeps losing assets to index funds
Revenue depends on market levels, so a bear market cuts fees directly
$1.0B of debt from acquisitions against $164M of cash
opportunities: A 25.3% net margin and $621M of free cash flow on $1.6B of revenue, among the best margins in asset management
Revenue grew from $821M to $1.3B in two years with the Amundi US deal
Analysts see about 13% upside, with 6 covering the stock
watch: Net client flows and the realised fee rate after the Amundi integration.
